name: AgenFetch Desktop
tagline: Windows local media downloader with optional browser extension and subtitle integration.
problem: Media downloading and conversion should be managed with explicit user consent, local tooling and truthful limits rather than collecting credentials through hosted intermediaries.
scenario: An authorized media URL entered directly or handed off from a Chrome/Edge extension opens in the local desktop download queue using the agenfetch:// protocol.
differentiation: The browser extension passes only a page URL to the installed app, while yt-dlp and optional subtitle integrations run under local user control with documented third-party boundaries.
architecture: Manifest V3 browser extension -> agenfetch:// OS protocol -> Electron desktop queue -> yt-dlp and FFmpeg -> user-selected filesystem output.
limitations: The beta does not bypass DRM or guarantee provider compatibility; users must have rights to download media and manually verify release integrity when installers are unsigned.
